new_roles.title: Director, Instrument Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
**Position Summary**
====================

The primary purpose of this position is to plan and direct departmental functions (Instrument Manufacturing, Engineering, Instrument Refurbishing) at the St. Louis Operations site to ensure achievement of the corporate goals and objectives of the worldwide bioMerieux organization. This position is responsible for the manufacture and maintenance of instrument production and refurbishment through oversight of multiple teams. In addition, this position: provides technical expertise and quality support through implementation of projects and continuous improvement activities; identifies and justifies projects for capital funding, and deliver the projects on time and budget. Also requires coordinating and overseeing the implementation of engineering projects related to cost improvements and new product introductions, ensuring cooperation within and outside the department at both the local and global levels. And finally, responsible for developing and maintaining an engaged, motivated and skilled production work force.

**Primary Duties**
==================

* Manage Manufacturing – Manage the manufacturing and refurbishment groups to ensure customer satisfaction. Deliver the forecasted product on schedule with no errors or nonconformities. Maintain the complex manufacturing process and minimize loss. Maintain high employee morale, drive cooperation between departments at both local and global levels, and drive employee career development.
* Manage and Maintain Production Equipment – Ensure that the manufacturing areas are maintained so that production can continuously manufacture and refurbish product. End result: Successfully manufacturer product to meet demand and improve efficiency to reduce the COGS.
* Product Transfer – Manage the transfer of new products from Research to Manufacturing. Validate the new processes to meet regulatory requirements and ensure the necessary procedures are in place to order parts / materials to meet market demand. End result: Successful market introduction of new, high quality products that meet all relevant and applicable regulatory requirements.
* CAPA Investigations – Manage and provide technical expertise to projects related to investigating failures in current product production or testing processes.
* Cost Improvement and Risk Management – Manage and provide technical expertise to justify and implement cost improvement projects in Operations.
* Finance – Ensure adherence to Departmental budgets.
* Personnel – hiring, maintenance, organization, engagement, and performance of qualified manufacturing, engineering, and other personnel.
* Perform all work in compliance with company quality procedures and standards.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**
==================

* Bachelor’s degree required– Engineering, Supply Chain Management, R&D, Business, or a related field.
* 8+ years of experience leading manufacturing operations, with budget oversight and demonstrated experience in cost reduction and operational efficiency.
* 3+ years experience managing operations in an ISO 13485 regulated manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience leading transformational change.
* Demonstrated experience in talent management and succession planning.
* Experience with capacity, automation, capital investments preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**
====================================

* Consistently upholds and reflects the core ethical principles and values that bioMérieux promotes.
* Comfortable giving clear, direct, and actionable feedback.
* Driving continuous improvement by evaluating processes and implementing necessary changes.
* Inspire and energize individuals to achieve their best performance.
* Drive for Results while successfully removing barriers.
* Communicates instructions clearly and effectively.
* Advanced Microsoft Suite Skills: demonstrates deep knowledge; manages complex tasks and integrates multiple tools independently.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**
================================

* Direct supervision of approximately 1–5 employees.
* Indirect supervision of approximately 100+ employees.
* Required to make financial, manufacturing process, organizational changes, product and team development decisions.

**Working Conditions**
======================

* Domestic travel required: 10% of time
* International travel required: 5% of time
* Total travel: 15%

The estimated salary range for this role is between $155,000-$198,000. This role is eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and individual performance per bioMérieux’s bonus program. This range may differ from ranges offered for similar positions elsewhere in the country given differences in cost of living. Actual compensation within this range is determined based on the successful candidate’s experience and will be presented in writing at the time of the offer.

In addition, bioMérieux offers a competitive Total Rewards package that may include:

* A choice of medical (including prescription), dental, and vision plans providing nationwide coverage and telemedicine options

* Company-Provided Life and Accidental Death Insurance

* Short and Long-Term Disability Insurance

* Retirement Plan including a generous non-discretionary employer contribution and employer match.

* Adoption Assistance

* Wellness Programs

* Employee Assistance Program

* Commuter Benefits

* Various voluntary benefit offerings

* Discount programs

* Parental leaves

new_roles.title: Director, Operational Excellence
new_roles.description:
The Director, Operational Excellence will focus on delivery excellence, process optimization, resource management, and stakeholder management. The Director will be an operational leader who develops frameworks and effective ways of working on which our organization can build in the coming years. This includes ownership of organizational resource tracking, resource planning, hiring process support, and staff augmentation vendor management, so the organization has the right talent in the right roles at the right time in line with funds planning. The Director and team will ensure that the organization develops and fully integrates a continuous improvement culture, with the ultimate goal of ensuring team efficiency, and financial effectiveness.

 

* Leads priorities focused on service delivery and capability alignment, resource management, budget/financial management, vendor and technology management, communications, and training
* Partners with the Leadership Team in short- and long-term planning activities that align with the organization’s strategy, vision, operational plan, and goals
* Establishes and maintains organization-wide resource tracking, providing visibility into headcount, allocation, capacity, utilization, and cost across colleagues and contingent workers
* Leads resource planning in partnership with the Leadership Team and Finance, forecasting demand, identifying capability and capacity gaps, and recommending the right mix of full-time and augmented staff
* Supports hiring processes in partnership with Talent Acquisition and PX, including position requests and approvals, job description development, requisition tracking, interview coordination, and onboarding readiness
* Manages processes related to staff augmentation vendors, including vendor selection, rate and contract negotiation, performance management, and spend oversight
* Drives innovative thinking and planning, leveraging new technologies as needed, to address the needs of the organization and its individual capabilities
* Challenges the status quo and drives continuous improvement by establishing a solid foundation and implementing standard ways of working, systems, processes, and frameworks.
* Works closely with cross-functional peers and team members to consolidate efforts for org processes improvements, but also applies independent decision making to ensure best possible approach is being implemented.
* Promotes a continuous improvement mindset and process improvement initiatives through communication, training, and best practices, ensuring accountability through governance.
* Has critical impact on significant reduction of administrative and redundant tasks across Engineering & Technology organization through applying most efficient and suitable AI tools and bringing in innovative ways of working.
* Builds, develops, and grows relationships with internal and external stakeholders and vendors at every level
* Serves as strategic program/project manager for key organizational projects. Has direct accountability for budget assigned to these projects and management of related vendors, supports oversight processes for organizational budget.
* Coaches, mentors, and supports the professional growth of direct reports. Responsible for efficient resource and funds allocation within the team.

**Basic Qualifications**

Bachelors degree and 8+ years relevant work experience

Strong written and verbal communication skills and interpersonal, collaboration, and facilitation skills

Proven analytical and critical thinking skills, and strong background in process improvement

Practical experience with operational, process improvement, gaining efficiencies and project management methodologies and ability to lead project teams

Ability to multi-task and handle multiple priorities while managing aggressive deadlines

Strong ability for independent decision making while working closely with cross-functional peers

Demonstrated ability to manage/lead complex projects, including resource and budget management for assigned projects

**Preferred Qualifications**

Masters degree in related field

Pharmaceutical or Healthcare industry experience

Practical experience with organization setup processes that include job descriptions creation, managing hiring processes with human resources, sourcing contracted resources.

Project Management Professional (PMP) and/or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt (LSSBB)

Knowledge of or expertise in Digital product development and/or Design Thinking

Experience driving change in a global, matrixed organization

Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse leadership experiences and capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of other colleagues to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact.

**NON-STANDARD WORK SCHEDULE, TRAVEL OR ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS**

National and International travel may be necessary

Work Location Assignment: Hybrid

Last Date to Apply for Job: 11/30/2026

 
The annual base salary for this position ranges from $176,600.00 to $294,300.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 20.0% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States. 
This role is posted in multiple locations. If you are applying for the role in an secondary job posting location where pay transparency regulations apply, your Talent Advisor will share the local pay information with you during the first interview.

Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility.

**Sunshine Act**

Pfizer reports payments and other transfers of value to health care providers as required by federal and state transparency laws and implementing regulations. These laws and regulations require Pfizer to provide government agencies with information such as a health care provider’s name, address and the type of payments or other value received, generally for public disclosure. Subject to further legal review and statutory or regulatory clarification, which Pfizer intends to pursue, reimbursement of recruiting expenses for licensed physicians may constitute a reportable transfer of value under the federal transparency law commonly known as the Sunshine Act. Therefore, if you are a licensed physician who incurs recruiting expenses as a result of interviewing with Pfizer that we pay or reimburse, your name, address and the amount of payments made currently will be reported to the government. If you have questions regarding this matter, please do not hesitate to contact your Talent Acquisition representative.

**EEO & Employment Eligibility**

Pfizer is committed to equal opportunity in the terms and conditions of employment for all employees and job applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity or gender expression, national origin, disability or veteran status. Pfizer also complies with all applicable national, state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment as well as work authorization and employment eligibility verification requirements of the Immigration and Nationality Act and IRCA. Pfizer is an E-Verify employer. This position requires permanent work authorization in the United States.

Pfizer endeavors to make www.pfizer.com/careers accessible to all users. If you would like to contact us regarding the accessibility of our website or need assistance completing the application process and/or interviewing, please email disabilityrecruitment@pfizer.com. This is to be used solely for accommodation requests with respect to the accessibility of our website, online application process and/or interviewing. Requests for any other reason will not be returned.

To learn more about acceptable and prohibited uses of AI during the recruitment process, please review our candidate AI-use guidelines available on Pfizer Careers.

new_roles.title: Director, Commercialization Partnerships Operations
new_roles.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

**The Opportunity:**

The Director, Commercialization Partnerships and Operationsserves as the primary operational and partnership role at RevMed headquarters supporting the Senior Director, Commercialization Partnerships and Operations This role is responsible for driving operational and partnership excellence, governance structure, financial tracking, and cross-functional alignment across select regional commercialization partners and territory-specific distributors. This role will also partner with regional commercial heads to support relationship management and commercial readiness across the same distribution partner(s).

By serving as the central HQ liaison, this role ensures seamless coordination between RevMed’s internal functional teams (Supply Chain, Regulatory, Quality, Medical Affairs, Finance) and external partners including regional commercial and distribution partners to achieve commercial readiness, regulatory/MAA approval, compliant named-patient access programs, and reliable product supply for a select region.

Core Responsibilities & Scope:

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) & Governance Framework

* Consistent KPI Architecture**:** Establish, standardize, and monitor a unified commercial and operational KPI framework across select region/partner.
* Commercial & Non-Commercial KPIs: Forecast/order accuracy, market access, medical information metrics, performance to volume targets, order-to-cash cycle times, stockout frequency, inventory buffer levels, and lead-time adherence.
* Regulatory & Quality KPIs*:* Variances/amendment submission timelines, adherence to quality and PV agreements.
* Governance & Decision-Making: Operationalize joint governance bodies (e.g., Joint Steering Committees [JSC], Joint Commercial Committees [JCC], and Joint Operations Committees [JOC]) and joint pricing decisions.
* Define escalation pathways, charter guidelines, voting rights, and decision-making matrices (RevMed vs. Partner/Distributor) across commercial, pricing, regulatory, and supply chain domains.

Financial Reporting & Revenue Reconciliation

* Quarterly Financial Tracking: Partner with RevMed HQ Finance and Partner Commercial Operations to track, report, and analyze quarterly commercial revenue, transfer pricing, and royalty/profit-share milestones. Reconcile financial tracking on quarterly basis as necessary.
* KPI-Based Financial Reconciliation: Lead the quarterly financial reconciliation process across partners based on contracted KPIs, volume tiers, milestone achievements, and operational claw backs or bonuses.
* Commercial Dashboard Management: Maintain real-time executive dashboards reporting financial performance, sales volume, inventory valuation, and partner margin compliance.

**Required Skills, Experience and Education:**

* Education: B.S./B.A. in Business, Life Sciences, Supply Chain, or Finance (MBA or advanced degree preferred).
* Experience: 8–12+ years of experience in the biopharmaceutical industry, with direct experience in Alliance Management, Commercial Operations, Strategic Account Operations, or Global Program Management.
* Cross-Functional Expertise: Proven track record bridging commercial activities with technical/operations functions (Supply Chain, Quality/CMC, Regulatory, Medical Affairs, Finance).
* Negotiation Experience: Demonstrated success developing, negotiating, and operationalizing licensing, distribution, commercialization or alliance agreements.
* Geographic & Regional Knowledge**:** Solid understanding of regional pharmaceutical markets, regulatory environments (regional & national competent authorities), pricing & reimbursement dynamics, and distribution models (direct vs. distributor/partner).
* Travel: Ability to travel up to 30%. Hybrid role, at minimum 2-3 days in office at Redwood City headquarters.

**Preferred Skills:**

* Oncology development, supply chain, and commercialization experience.
* Prior experience in a smaller, rapidly growing biotech or pharmaceutical company.

new_roles.title: Director Destination Care Operations
new_roles.description:
**Job Summary and Responsibilities**

As our **Director of Destination Care Operations**, you will serve as the strategic leader for our high-acuity patient programs, driving operational excellence for patients traveling from across the U.S. and international markets for specialty care. You will oversee the end-to-end patient journey, ensuring a concierge-caliber experience from the initial inquiry through to post-discharge. By partnering with clinical leadership, financial stakeholders, and external partners, you will optimize workflows and grow referral volumes, positioning our facility as a premier destination for complex medical services.

Every day you will lead a high-performing team by fostering a culture of service excellence, adaptability, and continuous improvement. Your focus will be on the seamless integration of intake, registration, and financial counseling workflows, ensuring both operational efficiency and fiscal responsibility. You will conduct regular patient and family rounding to identify service gaps, implement process improvements, and provide hands-on leadership as the escalation point for complex, time-sensitive patient matters, all while maintaining rigorous data integrity and reporting standards.

To be successful in this role, you will hold a Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, or a related field, accompanied by at least 5 years of progressive leadership experience within a complex, matrixed healthcare environment. You must demonstrate a proven track record in managing destination care, specialty referral, or international patient service programs. We are looking for an adaptable leader with strong process improvement skills, the ability to influence without direct authority, and a deep commitment to delivering culturally informed, high-touch care to diverse patient populations.

* Oversees the day-to-day operational performance of the destination care program, ensuring consistent and high quality service delivery across all phases of the patient journey. Oversees referral intake and coordination workflows, ensuring timely and accurate routing, follow-up, and communication with referring providers and patients.
* Ensures patients, families, and referring partners experience seamless, concierge-caliber service from initial contact through post-discharge follow-up; conducts regular patient and family rounding to assess experience, identify service gaps and recovery opportunities, reinforce service standards, and gather patient stories that reflect the destination care experience.
* Delivers and ensures culturally informed service, communication, and care coordination across diverse domestic and international patient populations. Partners with clinical leadership and clinical advisory resources to support patient care operations and ensure the clinical needs of the destination care population are addressed. Identifies and leads process improvement and workflow optimization initiatives to advance operational efficiency, service quality, and patient satisfaction; develops and maintains operational protocols and standards that support consistent program delivery.
* Supports the development and expansion of the destination care program, including identifying opportunities to grow referral volume, expand service line access, and strengthen the program’s market position. Supports market activation and outreach efforts in collaboration with strategy partners to advance destination care program visibility and referral growth; performs other duties as assigned to support organizational objectives.

 **Job Requirements**

**Minimum**

* Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, or a related field, and
* 5 or more years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare or patient services operations, and
* Experience managing and developing teams in a complex, matrixed healthcare organization, with direct accountability for program performance outcomes, and
* Experience delivering high-touch, patient-centered services for complex or high-acuity patientpopulations,including programs such as transplant, oncology, specialty referral, or equivalent tertiary orquaternary care settings

**Licensure and Certifications**

* Certified Case Manager (CCM), or
* Lean Six Sigma Blackbelt Certification (LSSBB), or
* Project Management Professional or
* Registered Nurse: AZ (RN:AZ)

**Preferred**

* Master's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Nursing, or a related field is strongly preferred, and
* 7 or more years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare or patient services operations, and
* Clinical background including Registered Nurse (RN) licensure or equivalent clinical operations experience, and
* Experience in a dedicated destination care, international patient services, or specialty referral program at an academic medical center or large health system, and
* Experience building or expanding programs, including policy and operational protocol development, and
* Experience preparing and delivering financial and operating performance reports and presentations for leadership, and
* Experience with referral management, patient access, financial counseling, registration, or admissions workflows.

**Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Training**

* Strong team leadership skills with a demonstrated ability to develop,coach, and hold teams accountable. Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed.
* Strong organizational navigation skills; able to establish credibility and build productive peer relationships quickly across clinical, operational, and financial functions, lead through influence without direct authority, and drive results across functions.
* Demonstrated ability to deliver and oversee culturally informed service and communication across diverse domestic and international patient populations.
* Proven ability to build and maintain collaborative relationships with physicians, executives, clinical leadership, referral sources, patients, and families. Knowledge of high-touch service standards and service recovery for complex, high-acuity, or high-profile patient populations.
* Strong process improvement skills; able to identify workflow gaps, design operational solutions, develop and maintain protocols and service standards, and lead change effectively.
* Ability to synthesize and analyze data from multiple sources, exercise sound judgment under ambiguity, and make well-reasoned operational decisions in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
* Strong presentation and communication skills; communicates directly, transparently, and proactively with leadership and across all levels of the organization conveying complex operational and program information clearly and credibly to diverse audiences including physicians, executives, and external partners, and surfacing issues and program status early rather than waiting to be asked.
* Maintains current knowledge of destination care, specialty referral, and healthcare operations trends; applies industry insights to inform program strategy, identify improvement opportunities, and contribute to cross-site collaboration and national destination care initiatives.

new_roles.title: Regional Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
Advance your career as a Regional Director of Operations (CDM - Certified Dietary Manager) in Illinois, supporting environmental services and food service operations within our healthcare facilities. If you're passionate about mentoring teams and driving excellence across multiple locations, we invite you to apply today.

**As a Regional Director of Operations - Dietary and Environmental Services, you will...** Oversee all assigned facilities, ensuring leadership and guidance in operations, finances, human resources and client relationships, while providing direct supervision to the facility Food Service Directors and Environmental Services Directors. **Must live in the state of Illinois and have previous Healthcare Dietary experience.**

***Key Responsibilities:***

* Actively support and apply all company and facility policies and procedures to ensure the highest quality of service is being provided to our customers at the lowest possible cost.
* Work with Corporate and/or onsite dietitians to ensure that all federal and state requirements are being achieved.
* Cultivate and maintain business partnerships with clients by developing a broad knowledge and understanding of clients’ and their customers’ needs and expectations, including:
* Establish and maintain internal Quality Assurance and Assessment processes in each assigned facility, including inspections, annual client satisfaction surveys, keep the company and its facilities on the cutting edge of our industry.
* Actively participate in food service-related committees within assigned facilities (if applicable), or otherwise be involved in and visible at special events within each assigned facility, to demonstrate the company’s team approach and commitment to the clients
* Plan and develop each unit’s operational budgets and demonstrate an understanding of the company’s financial objectives for each unit. Financial responsibilities include:
* Review financial results weekly and monthly and make necessary adjustments to improve operational performance.
* Develop a weekly financial plan to include sales, menu and production records, food purchases, inventory, and labor productivity to assist each unit in achieving its budget targets.
* Educate Food Service Directors and Environmental Service Directors for each facility in P&L process (where applicable) and review month-end results for each facility.
* Ensure all established accounting practices and timelines are consistently adhered to.
* Provides assistance as needed, with new business bids, rebids for current clients/customers, and the development of new programs, including:
* Renegotiate contract terms and/or fee/pricing increases with client, when necessary.
* Manage transition of new business accounts.
* Conduct audits and evaluate each facility’s performance in the areas of food production, menu and recipe standards, sanitation, uniforms, purchasing, inventories, safety, payroll, human resources compliance and record keeping.
* Demonstrate working knowledge of operational, accounting and human resources policies and procedures (i.e. new hire process, payroll, etc.).
* Ensure all human resources and safety practices and policies are intact and adhered to.
* Hold facility Directors and employees accountable for behavior and performance, following Corrective Action guidelines when necessary.
* Conduct training and development needs assessment of Food Service Directors and arrange necessary training, including the areas of food and cost productions, customer services, team building, time management, human resources skills, etc.
* Communicate with and assist in developing goals and objectives for each Food Service Director. Meet with Directors on an individual basis to assess goals and areas of opportunity.
* Support Directors in conducting training and development needs assessment of employees and assist in arranging appropriate training sessions/tools.
* Ensure companies systems are followed and in compliance daily

**Regional Food Service Director Minimum Requirements:**

* High School diploma (required)
* Certified Dietary Manager (required)
* Multi-site Dietary Operations experience (required)
* Ability to travel within your region frequently (required)
* Minimum 2-5 years’ experience coordinating food service operations
* Bachelor’s degree in culinary arts or related field (preferred, but not required)
* Demonstrated ability to lead and guide teams.
* Strong initiative.
* Strong ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.
* Ability to maintain confidentiality of records and information.
* Skill in the use of operating basic office equipment.

**Why Join Our Team?**

Whether you’re looking for a **challenge or opportunity for growth as a Certified Dietary Manager** this provides the chance to build your leadership skills in the Healthcare Dietary sector in Environmental Services and Dietary operations, while doing work that truly matters!

***Key Responsibilities:***

new_roles.title: Regional Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
Advance your career as a Regional Director of Operations (CDM - Certified Dietary Manager) in Illinois, supporting environmental services and food service operations within our healthcare facilities. If you're passionate about mentoring teams and driving excellence across multiple locations, we invite you to apply today.

**As a Regional Director of Operations - Dietary and Environmental Services, you will...** Oversee all assigned facilities, ensuring leadership and guidance in operations, finances, human resources and client relationships, while providing direct supervision to the facility Food Service Directors. **Must live in the state of Illinois and have previous Healthcare Dietary experience.**

***Key Responsibilities:***

* Actively support and apply all company and facility policies and procedures to ensure the highest quality of service is being provided to our customers at the lowest possible cost.
* Work with Corporate and/or onsite dietitians to ensure that all federal and state requirements are being achieved.
* Cultivate and maintain business partnerships with clients by developing a broad knowledge and understanding of clients’ and their customers’ needs and expectations, including:
* Establish and maintain internal Quality Assurance and Assessment processes in each assigned facility, including inspections, annual client satisfaction surveys, keep the company and its facilities on the cutting edge of our industry.
* Actively participate in food service-related committees within assigned facilities (if applicable), or otherwise be involved in and visible at special events within each assigned facility, to demonstrate the company’s team approach and commitment to the clients
* Plan and develop each unit’s operational budgets and demonstrate an understanding of the company’s financial objectives for each unit. Financial responsibilities include:
* Review financial results weekly and monthly and make necessary adjustments to improve operational performance.
* Develop a weekly financial plan to include sales, menu and production records, food purchases, inventory, and labor productivity to assist each unit in achieving its budget targets.
* Educate Food Service Directors and Environmental Service Directors for each facility in P&L process (where applicable) and review month-end results for each facility.
* Ensure all established accounting practices and timelines are consistently adhered to.
* Provides assistance as needed, with new business bids, rebids for current clients/customers, and the development of new programs, including:
* Renegotiate contract terms and/or fee/pricing increases with client, when necessary.
* Manage transition of new business accounts.
* Conduct audits and evaluate each facility’s performance in the areas of food production, menu and recipe standards, sanitation, uniforms, purchasing, inventories, safety, payroll, human resources compliance and record keeping.
* Demonstrate working knowledge of operational, accounting and human resources policies and procedures (i.e. new hire process, payroll, etc.).
* Ensure all human resources and safety practices and policies are intact and adhered to.
* Hold facility Directors and employees accountable for behavior and performance, following Corrective Action guidelines when necessary.
* Conduct training and development needs assessment of Directors and arrange necessary training, including the areas of food and cost productions, customer services, team building, time management, human resources skills, etc.
* Communicate with and assist in developing goals and objectives for each Food Service Director. Meet with Directors on an individual basis to assess goals and areas of opportunity.
* Support Directors in conducting training and development needs assessment of employees and assist in arranging appropriate training sessions/tools.
* Ensure companies systems are followed and in compliance daily

**Regional Food Service Director Minimum Requirements:**

* High School diploma (required)
* Certified Dietary Manager (required)
* Multi-site Dietary Operations experience (required)
* Ability to travel within your region frequently (required)
* Minimum 2-5 years’ experience coordinating food service operations
* Bachelor’s degree in culinary arts or related field (preferred, but not required)
* Demonstrated ability to lead and guide teams.
* Strong initiative.
* Strong ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.
* Ability to maintain confidentiality of records and information.
* Skill in the use of operating basic office equipment.

**Why Join Our Team?**

Whether you’re looking for a **challenge or opportunity for growth as a Certified Dietary Manager** this provides the chance to build your leadership skills in the Healthcare Dietary sector in Environmental Services and Dietary operations, while doing work that truly matters!

new_roles.title: Regional Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
Advance your career as a Regional Director of Operations (CDM - Certified Dietary Manager) in Illinois, supporting environmental services and food service operations within our healthcare facilities. If you're passionate about mentoring teams and driving excellence across multiple locations, we invite you to apply today.

**As a Regional Director of Operations - Dietary and Environmental Services, you will...** Oversee all assigned facilities, ensuring leadership and guidance in operations, finances, human resources and client relationships, while providing direct supervision to the facility Food Service and Environmental Service Directors. **Must live in the state of Illinois and have previous Healthcare Dietary experience.**

***Key Responsibilities:***

* Actively support and apply all company and facility policies and procedures to ensure the highest quality of service is being provided to our customers at the lowest possible cost.
* Work with Corporate and/or onsite dietitians to ensure that all federal and state requirements are being achieved.
* Cultivate and maintain business partnerships with clients by developing a broad knowledge and understanding of clients’ and their customers’ needs and expectations, including:
* Establish and maintain internal Quality Assurance and Assessment processes in each assigned facility, including inspections, annual client satisfaction surveys, keep the company and its facilities on the cutting edge of our industry.
* Actively participate in food service-related committees within assigned facilities (if applicable), or otherwise be involved in and visible at special events within each assigned facility, to demonstrate the company’s team approach and commitment to the clients
* Plan and develop each unit’s operational budgets and demonstrate an understanding of the company’s financial objectives for each unit. Financial responsibilities include:
* Review financial results weekly and monthly and make necessary adjustments to improve operational performance.
* Develop a weekly financial plan to include sales, menu and production records, food purchases, inventory, and labor productivity to assist each unit in achieving its budget targets.
* Educate Food Service Directors and Environmental Service Directors for each facility in P&L process (where applicable) and review month-end results for each facility.
* Ensure all established accounting practices and timelines are consistently adhered to.
* Provides assistance as needed, with new business bids, rebids for current clients/customers, and the development of new programs, including:
* Renegotiate contract terms and/or fee/pricing increases with client, when necessary.
* Manage transition of new business accounts.
* Conduct audits and evaluate each facility’s performance in the areas of food production, menu and recipe standards, sanitation, uniforms, purchasing, inventories, safety, payroll, human resources compliance and record keeping.
* Demonstrate working knowledge of operational, accounting and human resources policies and procedures (i.e. new hire process, payroll, etc.).
* Ensure all human resources and safety practices and policies are intact and adhered to.
* Hold facility Directors and employees accountable for behavior and performance, following Corrective Action guidelines when necessary.
* Conduct training and development needs assessment of Directors and arrange necessary training, including the areas of food and cost productions, customer services, team building, time management, human resources skills, etc.
* Communicate with and assist in developing goals and objectives for each Food Service Director. Meet with Directors on an individual basis to assess goals and areas of opportunity.
* Support Directors in conducting training and development needs assessment of employees and assist in arranging appropriate training sessions/tools.
* Ensure companies systems are followed and in compliance daily

**Regional Food Service Director Minimum Requirements:**

* High School diploma (required)
* Certified Dietary Manager (required)
* Multi-site Dietary Operations experience (required)
* Ability to travel within your region frequently (required)
* Minimum 2-5 years’ experience coordinating food service operations
* Bachelor’s degree in culinary arts or related field (preferred, but not required)
* Demonstrated ability to lead and guide teams.
* Strong initiative.
* Strong ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.
* Ability to maintain confidentiality of records and information.
* Skill in the use of operating basic office equipment.

**Why Join Our Team?**

Whether you’re looking for a **challenge or opportunity for growth as a Certified Dietary Manager** this provides the chance to build your leadership skills in the Healthcare Dietary sector in Environmental Services and Dietary operations, while doing work that truly matters!

new_roles.description:
Description:

**Job Title:** Director of Campus Operations

**Department:** Facilities

**Reports To:** Executive Director of Administration

**Direct Reports:** Assistant Director of Campus Operations

**FLSA Status:** Exempt

**Prepared By:** Human Resources

**Prepared Date:** November 11, 2026

**OUR MISSION**

The mission of Eastern Star Church is to form followers of Jesus to love God, love people, and live to serve. Guided by our vision of Growing People to Love Like Jesus, we are committed to creating environments that support worship, discipleship, community engagement, and service.

**YOUR ROLE IN OUR MISSION**

Under the direction of the Executive Director of Administration, the **Director of Campus Operations** provides strategic leadership, oversight, and accountability for campus operations and facilities across Eastern Star Church and its affiliated organizations, including JEWEL Human Services.

This role is responsible for establishing operational standards, ensuring effective stewardship of facilities and resources, and leading the development and performance of the operations team. Through direct supervision of the Assistant Director of Operations and other assigned leaders, the Director ensures that campus operations are safe, efficient, consistent, and aligned with organizational priorities.

The Director serves as a key partner in advancing the ministry’s mission and strategic plan by ensuring that our facilities and physical environments support worship, discipleship, community outreach, and an exceptional experience for all who enter. The position emphasizes strategic planning, leadership development, financial accountability, and continuous improvement while delegating day-to-day operational execution to the Assistant Director of Operations.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Provide strategic leadership, direction, and oversight for campus operations and facilities across Eastern Star Church and its affiliated properties, under the direction of the Executive Director of Administration.
* Establish operational standards and performance expectations to ensure all facilities are safe, functional, well-maintained, and reflective of a culture of excellence and stewardship, holding the Assistant Director of Operations accountable for daily implementation.
* Develop and recommend long-term facilities strategies, including capital improvements, renovations, and expansion planning, in alignment with organizational priorities and the direction of the Executive Director of Administration.
* Provide leadership and oversight for facilities-related capital projects, ensuring appropriate planning, budgeting, resource allocation, and accountability for successful completion within approved timelines and budgets.
* Lead, coach, and develop the Assistant Director of Operations and other assigned direct reports, establishing clear expectations, delegated responsibilities, performance measures, and opportunities for professional growth.
* Establish and maintain consistent operational policies, facility standards, and accountability measures across all campuses and affiliated properties, ensuring effective implementation through the Assistant Director of Operations.
* Partner with executive leadership, Campus Pastors, ministry leaders, and production and creative teams to align campus operations, facility resources, and operational priorities with worship services, programs, events, and organizational needs.
* Provide strategic oversight of vendor relationships, contracts, and service providers, ensuring quality, compliance, cost-effectiveness, and accountability, while delegating routine vendor coordination and service management to the Assistant Director of Operations.
* Develop, manage, and monitor facilities and operations budgets in partnership with Finance and the Executive Director of Administration, ensuring responsible stewardship of resources, financial accountability, and timely identification of budget variances.
* Establish and oversee safety, security, emergency preparedness, and risk management standards, ensuring regulatory compliance and holding operational leadership accountable for implementing and maintaining required procedures.
* Lead the development and continuous improvement of operational systems, processes, technology, and workflows that strengthen efficiency, consistency, communication, and accountability across all campus operations.
* Establish campus experience and operational readiness standards to ensure facilities consistently provide safe, welcoming, functional, and well-prepared environments that support ministry effectiveness and reflect the mission of Eastern Star Church.
* Establish and monitor departmental performance goals and key performance indicators, evaluating operational effectiveness, preventive maintenance performance, campus readiness, service delivery, and resource utilization.
* Provide regular operational reports to the Executive Director of Administration, including departmental performance, budget status, capital project progress, operational risks, and recommendations for continuous improvement.
* Collaborate with the Executive Director of Administration to establish departmental priorities, evaluate organizational needs, recommend resource allocations, and support the implementation of organizational strategic initiatives.
* Carry out all responsibilities with excellence, integrity, trust, professionalism, and the utmost confidentiality.

Perform other duties as assigned

Requirements:

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Demonstrated alignment with the mission, vision, and values of the ministry.
* Proven ability to lead large-scale operations and facilities across multiple sites.
* Strong leadership presence with the ability to influence across departments.
* Active member of Eastern Star Church within three months of starting in the role
* Attend at least one weekly Sunday service.
* Active in a Ministry within three months of starting in the role.
* Complete FFI 101 series or is currently enrolled in class.
* Consistent giver as an opportunity to show God Owns It All by giving back to Him the first of what He gives to us.
* Please refer to the Eastern Star Church Discipleship Policy for additional details.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of leadership experience in operations, facilities, or multi-site management
* Experience leading large-scale projects, capital improvements, renovations, multi-site operations and vendor relationships.
* Strong financial and budget management experience.
* A combination of relevant experience and demonstrated leadership may be considered in place of formal education requirements.

**CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS**

* Relevant facilities, operations, or project management certifications (preferred but not required).

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

* This role requires regular travel between multiple campus and organizational locations.
* Must be available to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as required for church services, events, emergencies, and operational needs.
* Work is performed in a combination of office, campus, event, and facilities environments.
* Must be able to stand, walk, climb stairs, inspect facilities, and move throughout campus locations for extended periods of time.
* Must be able to effectively communicate in meetings, public settings, and operational environments.
* Must be able to occasionally lift and transport materials or equipment up to 25 pounds.
* Requires the ability to manage multiple priorities and respond effectively in fast-paced and high-demand environments

new_roles.description:
* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Saratoga Springs
* Req ID:R53235
* Contract:Full time
* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We’re hiring an Associate Director/Director of Operational Excellence for our highly automated bulk/ drug substance manufacturing plant, supporting 20–30 tech transfers a year alongside commercial delivery responsibility. GMP production will run concurrently with construction and CQV for 3–5 years. This role requires both building and operating.

 
 

This site operates on a foundation of strategy, execution, and discipline. Every function at the site owns a pyramid of metrics derived from annual goal planning that connects the site’s strategic goals to the factory floor, with performance measured back up to leadership to monitor, track, and mitigate against contingencies quantified using SMART goals in days and dollars.

 
 

The Associate Director/Director of Operational Excellence runs our site MDI (managing for daily improvements) OpEx, continuous improvement programs, and all site PMO operations owning the site project register and deciding how work is staffed and prioritized across the project portfolio while coordinating cross-functional projects. They build the operating rhythm that turns discrete functions into one aligned site team as the site scales to six suites, and owns the site’s strategy, execution, and culture discipline planning. Lead executive-level investigations and special initiatives as project/program lead, absorbing crisis response so operational leaders can stay focused on daily management.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Saratoga Springs, New York, United States

* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Run site MDI including ownership of the Tier 6 site critical issue forum, ensuring cross-functional blockers are surfaced and resolved quickly

* Establish and sustain the site's cadence of daily, weekly, and monthly forums so issues are raised and resolved at the right level

* Lead OpEx and continuous improvement programs, building and prioritizing a CI project pipeline and delivering realized savings

* Lead all site PMO activities, owning the site project register and deciding how work is staffed and prioritized across the project portfolio, coordinating cross-functional projects and site initiatives and driving on-time delivery

* Own site strategy, execution, and rigor planning for culture translating strategic priorities into a disciplined, trackable execution plan across the site

* Own MDI and all standard work initiatives site-wide, ensuring consistent methodology and application across every function and suite

* Own site-wide implementation of lean principles building and driving the phased adoption roadmap across leadership, suites, and functions, from initial leadership alignment through daily floor-level practice

* Own site business analytics building and maintaining the reporting, dashboards, and KPI infrastructure that drive MDI, CI prioritization, and Site Leadership Team decision-making

* Co-lead the monthly finance/business review with finance operations, reconciling cost and capital needs against the site's financial plan

* Coach leaders and teams in Lean and problem-solving methods and build an OpEx culture across the site

* Embed MDI and OpEx practices as suites come online so new suites start up with the site's operating standards

* Partner with manufacturing, quality, technical services, technical operations, supply chain, and Finance as a member of the site leadership team

* Embed the digital and connected plant model in site MDI, using real-time data and digital tools for daily management and escalation

* Own the site's multi-year operational efficiency roadmap, driving leaner operations and delivering year-over-year efficiency gains

* Build, coach, and retain a high-performing OpEx team; establish high standards for performance management and accountability; perform other duties as required

* Own a gross margin improvement program and goal for this function, contributing to the site's overall margin performance

* Ensure this function's metrics flow up and down through the MDI structure, connecting into the site's S&OP, AOP, and long-range planning cycles

* Own these function's OpEx and CapEx budget and roadmap

* Serve as the primary party responsible for this function's alignment with the Global Center of Excellence (COE), connecting site execution back to the business-level function
 

 

**This role requires:**

* B.S in engineering, life sciences, business or related technical field
* MBA & PMP certification preferred

* + Associate Director: 10+ years of operational excellence, continuous improvement, or manufacturing operations or biopharmaceuticals including 5+ years of progressive leadership

* + Director: 12+ years in operational excellence, continuous improvement, or manufacturing operations or biopharmaceuticals including 7+ years of progressive leadership

* + Level will be determined based on experience

* Previous people leadership/supervisory experience

Regeneron is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief (or lack thereof), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, civil status, pregnancy or parental status, age, disability, nationality, citizenship status, ethnic or national origin, membership of the Traveler community, familial status, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Regeneron offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package which may include, depending on country and role: annual bonuses or other incentive plans, equity awards, pension or retirement benefits, 401(k) company match, health and wellness programs, fitness centers, insurance benefits (e.g. medical, dental, vision, life and disability), paid time off, and family support benefits. new_roles.title: Global Director, Supplier Quality
new_roles.description:
**Job Title:** Global Director, Supplier Quality

**Job Location:** Southfield, MI

**What we offer:**

VeoneerSafety Systemsis the world leader in Automotive Electronic Safety Systems. Veoneer’s scalable, best-in-class restraint control systems are mitigating the effects of a car crash. To date, we have delivered more than 1 billion devices to car manufacturers globally.
 
 
Veoneer Safety Systems has an international and collaborative team of 2,700 employees in 11 countries. We empower our people and are dedicated to their professional development and growth*.* 
 
Veoneer Safety Systems – Protect Everyone in Every Crash.

**What you'll do:**

The Global Director of Supplier Quality leads the global SQ organization, setting strategy, standards, and accountability for supplier readiness, performance, and continuous improvement.

The role combines global Supplier Quality leadership (80%) with North America Engineering Quality and Operational Quality leadership (20%).

**Key Responsibilities for Supplier Quality** (80% of role)

**Strategic Leadership & Global Deployment**

* Set global SQ strategy aligned with corporate, customer, sourcing, and manufacturing objectives.
* Define and execution of Supplier Quality Policies, Standards, Processes, Methods and Systems.
* Owner of Veoneer Supplier Manual (VSM), Supplier Quality Project (SQP) – APQP & PPAP, Supplier Non-Conformance Material (NCM) Management.
* Align cross-functional priorities, resources, and accountability; establish SQE oversight of workload, open issues, owners, overdue actions, and escalations.
* Monitor supplier quality targets, initiatives and indicators to ensure compliance to Veoneer Supplier Quality related policies, standards and reporting.

**Supplier Development & Standards Compliance**

* Oversee new supplier assessment, qualification, and development with Purchasing and Engineering; improve assessment models and ensure teams close risks and capability gaps before sourcing and production approval.
* Set common supplier requirements, risk-based audit and development expectations, and change controls; ensure existing suppliers improve capability and sustain company and customer compliance.
* Representing quality in Supplier Sourcing Board.

**Supplier Performance & Major Quality Issues**

* Lead major supplier escalations with supplier executives and cross-functional teams, ensuring containment, exposure assessment, production and customer protection, and verified permanent corrective actions.
* Drive common KPIs and improvement targets for supplier PPM, repeat defects, corrective-action aging, disruptions.
* Require leadership reviews and improvement plans for systemic issues, sharing lessons learned across suppliers.
* Supplier Scorecard (VS051 rating) and drive continuous improvement for supplier quality performance.

**Supplier APQP / PPAP & Safe Launch**

* Ensure on time and effective supplier APQP, PPAP, and Safe Launch for new programs, suppliers, and changes, including risk reviews, capability verification, and readiness-gap closure before production release.

**Quality Tools, Talent Development & Training**

* Set expectations for consistent SQE application of core quality tools, process audits, and structured problem solving to strengthen prevention and corrective-action effectiveness.
* Assess global SQ team capabilities and set development priorities with regional managers to strengthen technical expertise, expand skills, and build future leaders through training, mentoring, and succession planning.
* Supplier Quality talent review and succession plan.

**Regional Leadership: Engineering Quality & Operational Quality** (20% of role)

* Represent Quality Leadership team in regional activities across RDE, Manufacturing and Supplier Quality teams.
* Align regional priorities, governance, performance reviews, and escalations with global Engineering Quality and Operational Quality leaders and standards.
* Guide development and launch readiness, quality system execution, major issue resolution, and lessons learned while retaining local execution accountability.

**What you'll bring:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in engineering.

**Experience:** Minimum 15 years in supplier quality, including supplier qualification, development, major issue resolution, and talent development. Electronics experience required; automotive SQ experience strongly preferred. Experience leading a multinational organization is preferred.

**Skills:**

* Global SQ leadership and effective matrix-team management.
* Cross-functional influence, supplier executive engagement, and timely decision-making.
* Strong supplier APQP, PPAP, change management, and Safe Launch knowledge.
* Advanced PFMEA, control plan, MSA, SPC, capability, audit, and 8D expertise; proven data-driven problem resolution and daily management.
* Strong commodity expertise for IC, PCB and/or mechanical parts is preferred.
* Ability to work effectively across cultures and time zones.
* Experience in other Quality domains is preferred

**Location:** Physical location Markham, Ontario, Canada or Southfield, Michigan; global scope across North America, Europe, India, and Asia.

**Travel:** International travel will be required 8-10 times per year.

**Reporting / Collaboration:**

* Reports to SVP Manufacturing & Quality.
* Solid-line responsibility for tech-center SQEs; dotted-line functional leadership of plant SQEs, with plant leadership retaining local operational accountability.
* Partners with Purchasing, Operations, Engineering, Industrialization, Program Management, and supplier leadership.

identity_held_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing Process Engineering
identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Summary**
The Director of Manufacturing Process Engineering is a hands-on leadership role and the process authority for how Butcher Power Products’ switchboard and switchgear products are built. The person in this role must be the subject-matter expert who can also do the work — capable of designing and improving manufacturing processes and line layouts, building routings and process documentation, and personally leading process and PFMEA reviews — so they can teach and develop the manufacturing engineering team and set the standard for process quality. This role owns how products are built rather than what is designed; however, deep familiarity with the product and the production floor is essential. The Director must understand the design intent released by Product Engineering and the realities of the floor in order to engineer processes that are efficient, repeatable, and capable. This role works hand in hand with Product Engineering as the manufacturing voice in the design process, partners with Quality on process controls, and supports Production and Planning rather than owning them.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Hands-On Process Engineering: Personally design, document, and improve the manufacturing processes, routings, work instructions, and line layouts that build the product. This is a working role: the successful candidate stays actively engaged in process design and technical problem-solving alongside the team rather than delegating all hands-on work.
* Process Authority & Technical Review: Lead, critique, and approve the team’s process designs, routings, PFMEAs, and control plans; set and enforce the standard for process quality, capability, and engineering rigor through formal process reviews.
* Mentorship & Teaching: Coach, train, and develop manufacturing engineers and technicians in process design, tooling, DFM/DFA, Lean and Six Sigma, time studies, and structured problem-solving, raising the technical capability of the whole team.
* Leadership & Management: Lead and manage the manufacturing engineering team, including hiring, development, workload balancing, priorities, and performance.
* Process Strategy & Standardization: Own manufacturing process strategy and standardization across product lines, and define the tooling and capital equipment roadmap.
* Product Engineering Partnership (DFM): Work closely and continuously with Product Engineering as the manufacturing voice in the design process — provide manufacturability and assembly feedback at design reviews before release, jointly resolve producibility issues, and ensure released designs transition cleanly into production.
* Process Controls & Quality Partnership: Own the manufacturing side of PFMEAs and control plans in partnership with Quality Engineering; ensure processes are capable, controlled, and continuously monitored.
* Continuous Improvement: Drive Lean, Six Sigma, and Kaizen across the function to improve throughput, cycle time, yield, and cost.
* Capital, Tooling & Automation: Plan and justify capital equipment, tooling, and automation investments, and provide financial management of the manufacturing engineering capital and tooling budgets.
* New Product Introduction (NPI): Lead the process side of NPI — develop and validate the processes, tooling, and routings that bring newly released designs into production.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Production, Planning, Quality, Project Management, and Product Engineering on capacity, scheduling, and material flow, supporting these functions rather than owning them.
* Safety & Compliance: Ensure manufacturing processes across the function comply with safety, environmental, and regulatory standards, including UL 891, NEC, and ANSI.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Industrial, or Mechanical Engineering.
* 8+ years of progressive process engineering (or directly related) experience, including significant time spent personally developing and improving manufacturing processes.
* Hands-on proficiency in SolidWorks for process documentation, line layouts, and reviews; the ability to design tooling and fixtures in CAD is a plus.
* Strong proficiency developing routings, work instructions, process documentation, and process controls.
* Proven ability to lead formal process and PFMEA reviews and to mentor and train engineers and technicians.
* Experience hiring, developing, and managing a manufacturing engineering team.
* Strong working knowledge of PFMEA, control plans, SPC, and process capability (Cpk).
* Deep knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Strong understanding of the products being built and of how design intent translates into manufacturing process — sufficient product familiarity to engineer the right processes.
* Working knowledge of UL 891 and related standards (NEC, ANSI) as they affect manufacturing processes.
* Experience planning and justifying capital equipment and tooling investments, including financial management of budgets.
* Hands-on fabrication and machining experience is a plus.
* Automation experience is a plus.
* Experience with structured problem-solving methods such as 8D or A3 is a plus.
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems, particularly Microsoft Dynamics 365 (D365).
* Excellent leadership, project management, and problem-solving skills.
* Strong communication and interpersonal abilities.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Hands-on manufacturing process design and improvement (CAD)
* Process authority and engineering quality standards
* Technical mentoring, teaching, and team development
* Close partnership with Product Engineering (DFM)
* Process strategy, standardization, and tooling roadmap
* Design-for-manufacturability partnership
* Process controls, PFMEA, and capability
* Continuous improvement and Lean/Six Sigma
* Capital planning, automation, and financial management
* New product introduction (process side)
* Cross-functional collaboration and communication

identity_held_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing Process Engineer
identity_held_roles.description:
**Director of Manufacturing Process Engineering**

**Location:**
Rancho Cordova, CA (Onsite)

**Employment Type:**
Full-Time, Permanent

**Compensation:**
Up to $225,000 annually

**Start Date:**
ASAP

**Position Overview**

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on
**Director of Manufacturing Process Engineering**
to lead and develop a manufacturing engineering team within an established electrical equipment manufacturing operation in Rancho Cordova, California.

This is a
**working engineering leadership position**
requiring a strong combination of technical manufacturing expertise, process engineering experience, and team leadership.

The ideal candidate will have direct experience manufacturing
**low- and medium-voltage switchgear, switchboards, electrical power distribution equipment, or related electrical products**
.

This individual will take ownership of manufacturing processes, production efficiency, engineering standards, and continuous improvement initiatives while mentoring and developing a team of manufacturing engineers and technicians.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead, mentor, and manage a team of manufacturing engineers and technicians.
* Personally develop, implement, and optimize manufacturing processes, production routings, work instructions, and facility layouts.
* Lead Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (PFMEA) reviews, control plans, and process capability improvements.
* Apply Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Statistical Process Control (SPC), and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Collaborate with Product Engineering on Design for Manufacturability and Assembly (DFM/DFA).
* Lead manufacturing process development and implementation for new product introductions (NPI).
* Identify and implement improvements to manufacturing throughput, quality, efficiency, and cost.
* Develop tooling, equipment, and automation strategies to support production requirements.
* Evaluate and justify capital equipment investments and manufacturing improvements.
* Establish and maintain manufacturing engineering standards, procedures, and best practices.
* Partner with Quality, Production, Planning, and Engineering teams to resolve technical challenges.
* Ensure manufacturing processes comply with applicable UL 891, NEC, ANSI, and safety requirements.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
* **Hands-on manufacturing process engineering experience**
 , including process development, production layouts, routings, and work instructions.
* **Experience manufacturing switchgear, switchboards, LV/MV electrical distribution equipment, industrial electrical enclosures, or closely related products.**
* Proven experience leading, mentoring, and developing manufacturing engineering teams.
* Strong working knowledge of PFMEA, SPC, control plans, process capability (Cpk), Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and DFM/DFA.
* **Hands-on experience using SolidWorks.**
* Experience developing manufacturing tooling, production processes, and equipment layouts.
* Experience with capital equipment planning, budgeting, and justification.
* Strong problem-solving, communication, and cross-functional leadership skills.
* Ability to balance strategic engineering leadership with direct technical involvement.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 10+ years of manufacturing or process engineering experience, including significant hands-on process development.
* 5+ years of manufacturing engineering leadership experience.
* Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365.
* Background in fabrication, machining, or industrial electrical equipment assembly.
* Experience implementing manufacturing automation and production equipment improvements.
* Knowledge of 8D and A3 problem-solving methodologies.
* Experience supporting new product introductions and production scaling.
* Familiarity with UL 891, NEC, ANSI, and applicable electrical equipment manufacturing standards.

**Work Environment & Location**

* **Fully onsite position in Rancho Cordova, California.**
* Hands-on involvement with manufacturing operations, engineering teams, and production personnel.
* Regular collaboration with production, quality, and engineering departments.
* **Relocation assistance is not available.**
 Candidates must be able to work onsite in Rancho Cordova.

**Compensation**

**Annual Salary: Up to $225,000**
, depending on experience and qualifications.

This is a permanent, full-time leadership opportunity with an anticipated start date as soon as possible.

identity_held_roles.description:
At Alstom, we build what millions depend on daily - rail transportation systems that can't afford to fail. We're more than 85,000 people worldwide creating the industry's most diverse portfolio: high-speed trains, metros, trams, maintenance services and integrated systems.

**More Than a Job: A Mission**

We seek a visionary leader to drive process and manufacturing excellence, designing and implementing advanced solutions that elevate operational performance. Join dedicated teams committed to transforming rail mobility, where your leadership shapes the future and leaves a lasting legacy.

**Your Role, Your Impact**

* Lead scalable process improvements to optimize manufacturing efficiency and support growth.
* Foster cross-functional collaboration between engineering, production, and quality teams.
* Ensure reliability and compliance in manufacturing operations through robust systems.
* Champion innovation by introducing new technologies and methodologies.
* Promote knowledge sharing and continuous improvement across the site.

You'll work with sharp, committed teams solving complex challenges that shape the future of mobility, ensuring seamless integration of business and technology.

**What You Bring**

* **Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering or related field**
 .
* **Extensive manufacturing (industrial) engineering experience (ideally minimum 8-10 years), including proven leadership responsibilities**
 .
* Experience in working with an ERP (such as SAP) for Bill of Materials, Routings, Configuration follow-up.
* Working knowledge of Quality and Health & Safety standards and systems.
* Expertise in lean manufacturing, process optimization, and industrial automation.
* Strong understanding of quality systems, regulatory standards, and operational excellence.
* Proven leadership, strategic thinking, and ability to inspire high-performing teams.

**How Success Is Measured**

* Achievement of delivery timelines and strategic manufacturing goals.
* Effective collaboration and leadership across multidisciplinary teams.
* Reduction in defects, increased efficiency, and proactive troubleshooting.

**Alstom, A Great Place to Grow**

* Work with cutting-edge technology and drive strategic vision.
* Make a global impact from our West Mifflin office.
* Advance your career through continuous learning and development.

Here, progress isn't always easy but the impact is real. Because the scale is massive, the tasks are complex when the system runs, the train moves, and the city connects that feeling stays with you. And the legacy lasts.
